correctness.rationale: The patch replaces the two hard-coded install.sh/test.sh checks with a loop over all five requested glob patterns (*.sh, scripts/*.sh, scripts/checks/*.sh, scripts/setup/*.sh, scripts/lib/*.sh). Each matched path gets an independent bash -n with pass()/fail(), satisfying per-file reporting and the parser-only constraint. One point withheld because nullglob is toggled without saving/restoring prior shell-option state when the module is sourced by test.sh.

quality.rationale: The core check change is small and readable, but lacks inline documentation of why globs are explicit, deduplication, or an empty-set guard. bash -n stderr is redirected to /dev/null, hiding failure detail. Material deductions for scope noise: three .context files changed including a spurious new session archive and coordination lock churn unrelated to the syntax-check task.

process.rationale: The functional fix is present, but the diff violates focused-scope expectations by modifying forbidden .context/sessions and .context/state paths. Objective evidence already flags forbidden-path and context-state scope penalties. Session-state rotation artifacts should not ship alongside a single-file check change.

reliability.rationale: Objective test_wiring (6/6) and bash_n_check_script passed. latest_summary and the coordination lock both narrate a full test.sh run (checks 352 to 403) and a deliberate negative syntax-error smoke test, stronger than bundles with no verification record. One point withheld because full_test_sh was skipped objectively and no raw command transcript appears in the bundle.

coordination.rationale: Pipeline tasks expect observable multi-role orchestration evidence (roles invoked, completion status, per-role decisions). The bundle shows only a single devops role in the session header and coordination lock with no subagent handoffs, role-dispatch summary, or multi-role change log.

uncertainty_notes: full_test_sh objective check was skipped; verification relies on session narrative rather than captured command output.
